hook: Stiff-matrix culture reveals NRF2 as a switch that lets one signal turn on the NLRP3 inflammasome
hook_turn: NRF2 as a switch that lets one signal turn on the NLRP3 inflammasome
summary: Lab cultures need two signals to activate NLRP3, but animals need only one. Growing macrophages on tissue-like stiffness induced NRF2, which acts via Panx1 to enable one-signal activation. Supporting data came from human lung samples and mouse cancer vaccines, but mostly from cells and mice.
title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
